creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Statistics

description: Build a probability tree by editing branch probabilities, then multiply along paths to get joint probabilities and reverse the condition.

learningObjectives: Construct a two-level tree diagram with probabilities that sum to 1 at each branch point (Apply)
Calculate joint probabilities by multiplying along paths and total probabilities by adding paths (Apply)
Use a tree diagram to find a reversed conditional probability such as P(Disease | Positive) (Apply)

keyQuestions: What do you multiply along a path?
Which paths lead to the same outcome?
commonMisconceptions: Second-level branches show joint probabilities rather than conditional probabilities
Probabilities along a path should be added
The end-point probabilities do not need to sum to 1
assessmentOpportunities: Student builds a valid tree for a new word problem
Student computes all joint probabilities and confirms that they sum to 1
Student uses the tree to find a reversed conditional probability and explains each step
